ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6

candidates.why: The patient presented with chest pain and vomiting, and laboratory tests and imaging studies support the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.

candidates.name: Dextrocardia with Situs Inversus
support_spans: The maximal cardiac impulse was noted to be in the right fifth interspace
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
candidates.why: The patient's cardiac impulse and echocardiogram findings suggest dextrocardia with situs inversus, a congenital anomaly where the heart is on the right side of the chest.

candidates.name: Cor Pulmonale

candidates.why: The patient's hepatic dullness on the left side may indicate an enlarged liver due to right heart failure, which could be a sign of cor pulmonale.
